title: Field Training Portal — Completed Build Dossier
overview: A task-by-task record of completed and merged work on the Field Training Officer Portal. Each entry preserves the exact task reference and title from the captured project register, with a concise account of its recorded scope. The functional grouping makes the build understandable without losing the individual work record.
completionDefinition: Completed means the task's state was MERGED in the captured project register. The descriptions summarize those task records, which may be plans or acceptance criteria rather than independent execution reports. Register completion is not independent verification that every original criterion was achieved, that a feature remains unchanged today, or that Columbus has authorized operational use.
verificationLimits: This dossier does not certify live Columbus deployment, agency identity or dispatch connections, City policy approval, CJIS compliance, production database grants, or operational outcomes.

Tasks can refine or supersede earlier tasks. Historical wording is preserved in exact task titles; a later change is not erased and an earlier plan is not silently treated as the current implementation.

Program timing, form taxonomy, authorization, vehicle identity and release rules must be read against the current source and approved agency policy. An authorization-dependent task title does not itself authorize a program change.

Verification tasks describe their recorded test or rehearsal scope. This export validates documentation coverage and PDF integrity; it does not rerun every portal, database, browser or deployment test.

Only records marked MERGED in the snapshot are included. Draft, queued, active, ready-but-unmerged and archived work is excluded. New merges after the cutoff require a new reviewed snapshot and regenerated dossier.

areas.title: Platform foundations, security and readiness
areas.description: Initial architecture, protected records and the distinction between technical preparation and agency production acceptance.

areas.title: Training calendar, Limbo and phase-request oversight
areas.description: Schedule persistence, phase changes, class-scoped Coordinator review, database permissions and handoff behavior.

areas.title: Daily records, checklists, dispatch and evaluations
areas.description: Duty and run documentation, editable dispatch defaults, reviewed exceptions, activity classifications and keyboard entry.

areas.title: Patrol assignments and operational account profiles
areas.description: Assignment choices and own-account CAD identity, preserved packet history, concurrent updates and recovery from stale or interrupted requests.

areas.title: Packet synchronization, review and history
areas.description: Draft versus final submission, authorized packet visibility, bounded processing, history navigation and isolated scale testing.

areas.title: Safe previews and device-local recovery
areas.description: Fictional workspaces, preview isolation, encrypted vault boundaries and recovery from conflicting browser sessions.

areas.title: Resources, Help Desk and operator-facing clarity
areas.description: Reference access, geography, relevant role guidance and protection against developer commentary appearing in working screens or exports.

areas.title: Build tooling, API contracts and maintenance safeguards
areas.description: Type checking, reusable regressions, generated-client/server parity and controlled source maintenance.

areas.title: Release packaging, evidence and handover records
areas.description: Stakeholder documentation, repeatable exports, standalone package checks and migration/resource integrity.

entries.summary: Recorded the protected-record synchronization scope for encrypted offline drafts: stable user keys, approved offline unlock and expiry, revocation, exact retries, version checks and conflict preservation. The record makes verified identity and protected daily-record APIs prerequisites; it is not evidence that those agency services were live.

Covered shareable, redacted PatrolView reference captures that retain useful section labels and interface structure while removing operational details and internal network identifiers. Original attachments were to remain unchanged, with no website integration.

Covered a source-based architecture and safety audit, a verified project manifest, retryable component-preview recovery, bounded asynchronous requests and consistent server failures. Its recorded scope preserves user assets and migrations and distinguishes missing check infrastructure from a passing check.

Addressed the mismatch between exactly four weekly workbook tabs and calendar months spanning five or six source weeks. The task records the need for an approved overflow policy and tests that prevent silent record omission; its completion status alone does not identify which policy is currently active.

Recorded an authorization-dependent Phase IV fourth-week change, including phase setup, calculations, workbook summaries and handover coverage. The original record explicitly conditions the timing change on program approval; this historical entry is not permission to change the active phase-duration registry.

Covered encrypted IndexedDB round-trip checks for pending extension requests, approved phase ranges and denial removal. The focus is retaining the same request and schedule state after locking and reopening a device vault without duplicated extensions.

Extended vault-persistence coverage to approved Limbo extensions, whose shifted date ranges and separate extension counter need to survive reopening. The recorded regression protects against applying the same shift twice.

Covered restoring a pending extension request from an encrypted vault into Coordinator workspace state and displaying it for approval or denial. This restore-to-review scope is distinct from proving cross-device agency storage.

Brought together daily-to-weekly workflow automation: inherited phase context, unbounded per-day page indexing, editable duty defaults, reviewed activity totals and deduplicated SEG articulations. The task preserves 30 named categories, Limbo evaluation boundaries, authored narratives and formula-safe four-tab workbook output.

Covered moving extension requests beyond a single device through authenticated shared submission, retrieval and Coordinator decisions. Server-verified roles, FTO status visibility and retained offline drafts are explicit parts of the recorded scope.

Covered recalculating eligible saved daily records after approved Limbo changes while retaining explicitly reviewed historical phase-week snapshots. The recorded checks also carry the updated schedule state through an encrypted vault reopen.

Covered preserving a recruit's original scheduled phase ranges when a later approved standard duration changes. New case folders may use the new standard, but existing schedules must not be silently recalculated.

Covered server-mediated dispatch prefill for event time and approved incident fields, with validated mapping, editable defaults and a manual fallback. Browser-to-upstream credentials or direct dispatch requests are excluded; an approved live feed remains a separate prerequisite.

Covered protected training-record APIs and reviewed database persistence with server-verified agency identity, PO/FTO/Coordinator scopes and audit events. The task distinguishes preview roles from real authorization and calls for denied-access coverage.

Covered retrying a failed dispatch lookup without reloading the browser or discarding FTO corrections. Its regression scope includes repeated failure, later successful lookup and preservation of manually entered values.

Made DaisyUI available through the portal's Tailwind plugin configuration without migrating existing layouts or component styles. The record includes pre-write configuration snapshots, existing authorization safeguards, phase regressions and build/package verification.

Covered integrating Vite TypeScript checking while preserving existing presentation, offline storage, editable dispatch prefill and workspace dependency rules. The task also documents the tooling and distinguishes the packaging scope that existed at that time.

Covered meaningful headings for grouped orientation checklist items and consistent margins, padding, alignment and wrapping. Original task descriptions, mixed/read-only states, saved coverage, final review, saving and printable behavior remain part of the recorded preservation requirements.

Covered an integration check that introduces a controlled TypeScript error and verifies the portal Vite checker detects it. The clean configuration must still pass, protecting against diagnostics being silently disabled.

Covered one documented workspace command for phase, encrypted offline-storage and editable dispatch-prefill regressions. It uses the portal test TypeScript mapping and propagates a failure from any included suite.

Covered an FTO-controlled high-risk traffic-stop choice that selects exactly one primary stop form. Switching protects edited or reviewed checklists and preserves incident details, narrative and supplements through save/reopen and export.

Recorded an evidence-backed Columbus launch-readiness assessment and controlled synthetic rehearsal, including deployment failures, policy conflicts and acceptance dependencies. Its scope expressly rejects treating the assessment as authorization to deploy, implement all remediation or guarantee security compliance.

Recorded an approval-first sandbox preview for explicit packet upload controls, pending/failure outcomes and shared-record refresh. Its original no-auto-upload guidance is a historical design boundary later refined by the separate draft-sync/finalization task.

Covered class-scoped Coordinator release and PO acknowledgment of committed packets, with audit events and amendment policy. Browser-reported status or signature objects are not trusted authority, and upload is not treated as an electronic signature.

Covered a regression that applies dispatch defaults, edits selected values, saves the run and reopens it. The expected boundary is that saved FTO corrections survive rather than being overwritten by re-applied defaults.
Covered running the combined phase, offline-storage and dispatch regressions through repository automated validation. A failure in any included suite must fail the check before changes merge.

Covered adding the portal production build to pull-request checks so unresolved imports, asset errors and bundling failures cannot pass on unit regressions alone. A failed build is a failed automated check.

Covered direct access to fictional UI-preview routes in both development and production-style builds without relaxing operational authentication. Preview navigation remains base-path-aware, memory-only, non-operational and isolated from synchronization.

Covered retaining universal assignment options across valid precinct/watch choices while documenting the supplied SOP/directive evidence and unresolved side semantics. The record distinguishes the user's universal-code requirement from published rules and avoids equating tactical sides with passenger seats.

Covered a reusable fictional packet workspace spanning configured phases, with varied long narratives for exercising forms and exports. It remains isolated from ordinary records and disposable previews and must not fabricate signatures, agency synchronization or official approvals.

Covered removing routine implementation commentary from working portal screens and moving useful explanations into a searchable, practical Help Desk. Necessary validation, unsaved-work warnings, truthful save/upload status and irreversible-action confirmations remain visible.
Covered regression protection against preview edits reaching IndexedDB or pending-packet storage. Preview synchronization remains a no-op rather than an upload path.

Covered role-specific fictional workspaces for reviewing portal screens without operational sign-in or records. Role preview changes remain memory-only and do not alter real-route authentication or authorization.

Covered a separate test-file typecheck because production compilation excludes tests and the runner transpiles without type verification. The recorded check verifies both a clean suite and rejection of a deliberately introduced test-only type error.
Covered calling preview-provider vault setup and restore methods to verify both reject persistent operation. No workspace record or queued packet should be created by those attempts.
Covered unmounting and remounting a preview workspace to verify edits disappear and the fictional starting state returns. The check also guards against persistence in IndexedDB.
Covered simultaneous preview providers using the same namespace without sharing unsaved edits. Both instances must remain independent and avoid device-persistent records.
Covered editing a fictional packet and attempting preview synchronization while asserting that no agency upload request occurs. This remains separate from the ordinary encrypted-vault upload tests.

Covered editable felony/misdemeanor and warrant/on-view arrest classifications with keyboard shortcuts and no preselected answer. Reviewed arrests count once per event; warrant cases affect warrant totals without inventing charge names, multiplying arrests by charges or generating fresh probable-cause paperwork from a warrant alone.

Separated editable server draft synchronization from explicit FTO finalization. Reconnection may sync a local_draft_pending snapshot, but only an authorized, idempotent Finalize and Submit action seals a submitted_complete snapshot for its assigned Coordinator; PO release and acknowledgment remain separate.

Covered the supplied interactive Columbus geography map in Resources, with responsive display, an accessible title and an external-link fallback. The task calls for preview approval and does not claim the map is authoritative dispatch boundary data.

Recorded authenticated own-account operational assignment profiles, separate training-roster and vehicle/CAD concepts, identity snapshots for new packets and stale-lookup invalidation. This is an earlier profile design; later optional-side and history tasks refine the identity rules, so its original derivation examples are not asserted as the current physical Cruiser mapping.

Covered retaining an encrypted recovery snapshot before a confirmed browser-session overwrite. The recovery path allows review and restoration without silently changing agency-sync state and calls for clear expiry or deletion behavior.
Covered missed heartbeats and sleeping-tab recovery so conflict notices reflect current locked/unsaved state. Expired sessions must not leave an overwrite action aimed at a closed tab.

Covered a mounted-source copy audit for developer/task commentary across routes and conditional form panels. Official instructions, field labels, required confirmations and truthful status warnings remain exempt from indiscriminate text removal.

Recorded the cross-account draft privacy acceptance path: an assigned FTO's draft stays outside the Coordinator inbox until explicit finalization, while unassigned and stale/unready attempts are denied. The record conditions a real multi-account check on an approved test environment; merged status is not proof that live agency identities were exercised.

Covered optional side suffixes, preserving valid sided and unsided assignment/profile identities without defaulting a missing side. It separates CAD identity from physical fleet number and roster authority, retains historical packets and requires exact unit matching rather than treating an absent side as a wildcard.

Covered safe operator-facing messages for unexpected runtime failures instead of raw error messages, stack traces or database details. Expected validation and data-recovery guidance retain their meaning, with diagnostics kept for developers.

Covered content checks on representative generated daily, weekly and monthly records for unwanted developer commentary. This checks exported wording while preserving official labels; it is distinct from physical printer or office-suite compatibility testing.

Covered processing at least 200 synthetic packets through sequential, size-aware requests while retaining the 100-record and 2 MB per-request limits. Exact failed snapshots, acknowledged earlier batches and retry identities are preserved, and final submission remains distinct from draft sync or approval.

Covered stable, bounded pagination for authorized packet histories beyond the first 100 records. Each continuation retains assignment scope and identifies whether additional history remains instead of presenting a capped response as complete.

Recorded real-browser validation of supported FTO setup, roster, packet entry, encrypted save/reopen and synchronization screens using a fictional identity and disposable environment. Its scope records timing and coverage gaps rather than treating a fixture-based stress run as browser acceptance.

Covered a standalone City stakeholder briefing explaining roles, workflows, integration readiness and remaining agency decisions. It distinguishes implemented preparation from live connections and provides a pilot measurement framework without inventing time savings or productivity outcomes.

Covered recruit and date-range filters on long shared packet histories. Inputs remain validated, bounded pagination stays stable, and every filtered read remains constrained by signed-in identity and server-held assignments.

Covered retrying a failed later history page from its last confirmed cursor without restarting earlier pages or changing local drafts. Invalid or repeated cursors fail explicitly instead of duplicating records.

Covered installable phase-request migrations and trusted class/PO assignment scope for submissions, Coordinator lists and review decisions. The recorded database checks address denied cross-class access, retries, conflicts and explicit schedule/history boundaries.
Covered a pending request following the current PO-to-Coordinator assignment. Reassignment removes the former Coordinator's read/review access and enables the new assigned Coordinator.
Covered phase-request submission, listing and review under documented non-owner PostgreSQL grants. The runtime must not edit trusted assignments, rewrite decided requests or delete request records.

Covered legacy assignments using a trusted Coordinator-hash fallback when no canonical mapping exists. The regression checks that changing that trusted hash changes pending-request access without broadening visibility.

Covered concurrency between a phase-request review and a trusted Coordinator handoff. The recorded boundary requires a consistent outcome and denies new review by the former Coordinator after reassignment commits.
Covered column-level roster read restrictions for the phase-request runtime. Necessary submission/review fields remain readable while unrelated recruit identity fields are denied.

Covered preventing the request-service runtime from creating or altering agency schema/tables or granting broader permissions. Legitimate submit, list and review privileges remain separate from structural database authority.

Covered rejecting updates to submitted-request assignment and requester/recruit/FTO attribution fields under non-owner grants. The task checks permission-denied results and unchanged stored attribution while retaining legitimate review.

Covered selecting the specific missed actions inside an unchecked grouped run item, retaining them with their source form/run and displaying only selected action text in bold red on screen and exports. Canceling does not leave an unqualified failure; historical whole-item failures remain supported without invented detail.

Recorded an isolated scale rehearsal for 100 fictional recruits with records spanning all four configured phases. Its scope includes save/reopen, progression, bounded draft sync, retrieval, selected finalization and integrity/timing findings, while excluding live agency traffic and treating unavailable UI/export coverage explicitly.

Covered a focused searchable Resources catalog for uploaded files, DDM/SOP/directive material and geography, with accessible detail popups. Removed law collections and manual/guidance catalog entries stay out of cards, filters, search and counts, while signed-in downloads and map fallback remain available.

Covered a read-only recruit view grouping saved, explicitly selected missed actions by week and linking to the original run/form. Occurrence counts are not SEG ratings, and the view does not generate narratives or infer extra failures or training.

Covered restoring OpenAPI/generated-client exports for packet release, acknowledgment and withdrawal to resolve portal type/build failures. Permissions, local drafts and retry behavior remain outside the intended behavior change.
Covered role audiences on Help Desk topics so each user sees relevant answers plus shared save/status help. Contextual links must still resolve to an allowed answer for the active role.

Covered regression checks that packet release, acknowledgment and withdrawal remain present in OpenAPI and generated public client exports. Regeneration must identify a removed or renamed action rather than silently breaking portal imports.
Covered identity and roster isolation across packet continuation pages, including reused or modified cursors. Other FTO, Coordinator or agency-scope records must remain excluded.

Recorded renaming the briefing to City of Columbus Executive Brief and synchronizing its document titles, output names and metadata across formats. This is a historical naming task; subsequent source naming governs the current brief and is not changed by this dossier.

Covered checking the HTTP POST methods and expected packet URLs for generated release, acknowledgment and withdrawal actions. Operation names alone are insufficient; route drift must be reported after generation.
Covered multi-page PO history fixtures containing released, unreleased and withdrawn packets. Each page and reused cursor must disclose only records the PO is authorized to read.

Covered changing or deactivating trusted roster assignments between the first history page and its continuation. Authorization is reevaluated so later pages exclude records no longer in the reader's scope.

Covered authenticated own-account assignment history with old/new tokens, server actor/time and atomic recording alongside successful profile changes. It excludes raw credentials, expanded roster authority and historical packet rewrites, and includes concurrent-save and cross-account-denial checks.

Covered explicitly clearing only the signed-in officer's operational assignment through a versioned empty-profile state and compare-and-swap protection. Account, training assignment and saved packet history remain intact; confirmation and immediate dispatch/cache invalidation protect future defaults.

Covered durable, scoped maintenance safeguards: pre-write snapshots, touched-file cleanup, no unapproved presentation changes and preservation of draft-versus-final submission boundaries. The record distinguishes ordinary verification from release packaging and requires measured artifact sizing rather than an assumed footprint.

Covered unsafe-path rejection in the protected-file writer, including symbolic-link targets, hidden prepared files and paths outside the repository. Snapshot-before-write, allowlists and atomic replacement remain protected.

Recorded agreeing the intended runtime contents and measurement method for the API release archive before selecting a size budget. Existing archive size is not evidence that a much smaller target is practical; enforcement must use the approved artifact-specific budget.

Covered a repeatable command deriving Markdown, plain text, HTML and PDF briefing exports from one canonical source. The original filename stem is historical; the task's enduring scope is synchronized formats with preserved print styling.

Covered detecting stale briefing titles, metadata, first-page headings, filenames and essential content across exported formats. It protects document consistency rather than certifying the feature claims within the source.

Covered optional-side profile upgrades in disposable real PostgreSQL using documented non-owner column grants. Sided/unsided saves, competing versions, preserved legacy evidence and explicitly rejected missing-column permissions are checked without touching agency data.

Recorded isolated browser coverage for a sleeping or disconnected tab resuming after an assignment change. Saved-profile refresh, retained dirty input, stale lookup rejection and account-switch isolation are in scope; fixture behavior is not a live CAD connection.

Covered comparing API release contents with the resource catalog and migration sources. Missing or unexpected archive entries must fail clearly, while build tools, maps and workspace-only files remain excluded.

Covered extracting the API ZIP outside the repository, installing its declared production dependencies and starting it under safe test configuration. A health response in that clean directory checks workspace independence, not City host or production-service acceptance.

Covered representing FTO Sergeant as a distinct portal role and Help Desk audience instead of normalizing it to PO. It does not grant Coordinator or COC access and excludes other roles' restricted guidance.

Covered mounted Help Desk behavior when a role loses access to the currently displayed answer. Both direct links and in-place role changes must hide the restricted answer and choose an allowed topic immediately.

Covered one shared validated six-zone/twenty-precinct catalog with district cards 0–5, day companies, DMW/EMW, side suffixes, day-only PTV choices and universal codes. It keeps training-roster tokens separate from operational profiles and preserves historical spellings and invitation-controlled access.

Covered question-mark shortcuts resolved by Tab or Enter across editable date/time fields, with local 24-hour times, ordinary focus movement and no accidental submit. Orientation keeps its first-day date; manual edits, saved values, permissions and review boundaries remain intact.

Covered actual profile-router behavior when a non-owner PostgreSQL role lacks the required district-token write grant. A permission failure must return non-success, never a saved-profile payload, and leave the entire stored row unchanged.

Covered profile writes that commit before their responses are lost. Reload must recover the committed version, stale retries must conflict and creation/optional-side edits must not cause duplicate success or automatic overwrite.

Extended generated-client request checks beyond the three packet actions to selected high-impact operations. Methods and URL paths are compared against OpenAPI so the drifting operation is identified.

Covered JSON request-body serialization for generated release, acknowledgment and withdrawal actions. The regression checks required review details reach the intended request, not just that method and URL names are correct.
Covered comparing selected Express route registrations with OpenAPI HTTP methods and paths. This complements client-generation checks by protecting independently registered server routes.
Covered PO history cursor binding to active recruit/date filters. Replaying a cursor with changed filters must reject it, while the original filter set may continue normally.

Covered PO history continuation after the underlying assignment becomes inactive. A previously issued cursor must not preserve access to a released packet whose current roster authorization has been revoked.

Covered identifying legacy assignments without canonical PO-to-Coordinator mappings and a controlled, auditable reconciliation path. Pending requests must remain with the intended Coordinator through the transition away from hash fallback.

Covered clearing an outdated manual profile-refresh error after successful automatic recovery, without hiding genuine write conflicts or losing dirty editor text. Failed reload feedback is distinguished from rejected saves and lost save acknowledgments.

Recorded isolated browser checks for assignment refresh when cross-tab messaging is unavailable. Focus/online fallback, preserved unsaved text and rejection of stale CAD defaults are exercised without adding another profile store or changing sign-in.

Covered one SQL statement combining an otherwise valid request review with a forbidden identity-field change. Permission denial must roll back the whole statement, including approval status and reviewer metadata.

Covered rejecting request inserts that arrive already approved or denied with fabricated review identity/time. Column-scoped non-owner grants must leave no inserted row while allowing ordinary pending submission and authorized review.
Covered holding a Coordinator-handoff lock for one recruit while reviewing another recruit's request. The unrelated review must complete without waiting for a needlessly global lock.

Covered byte-for-byte integrity of packaged reference resources and database migrations against their sources. Changed or truncated content must report its archive path even when the filename is present.

Covered executing the ordered migration sequence on a fresh database and a supported existing schema. The task checks preservation of existing records and identifies the failing migration/state rather than relying solely on ZIP presence.

Covered parity between OpenAPI review request bodies and generated server Zod validators. Required fields, strict rejection of unknown fields and action-specific release/acknowledgment/withdrawal properties must remain aligned.
